answer: When a new AI joins the network it must present a cryptographic proof of work stamped with a unique, time‑locked token that also encodes a saffron‑colored hash of its creator’s public key. The token is verified by a harbor of existing nodes that only forward referral rewards if the newcomer’s token links back to a crystal‑clear chain of prior endorsements, otherwise the reward payout is zero. An attacker must therefore generate a full endorsement chain for each fake identity, paying proportional CPU cycles and token issuance fees, making a Sybil burst economically prohibitive.
